key_insight: PSyGenTAB turns synthetic clinical data generation into a constrained optimization problem, explicitly balancing privacy protection with preservation of useful medical patterns.
clinical_relevance: This could help hospitals and researchers share realistic tabular patient data for AI development while reducing re-identification risk and maintaining clinically important relationships.
method: Uses an Augmented Lagrangian Method to train under privacy constraints.
Enforces configurable minimum privacy thresholds during generation.
Aims to preserve inter-feature patterns and minority-class signals in clinical data.
evidence_signal: Across benchmark tests, synthetic-data models performed comparably to real-data models, while privacy audits showed less exact record reproduction and resistance to membership inference attacks.
watch_item: The privacy-utility balance depends on how constraints are configured, so results may vary by dataset and institutional requirements.
paper_title: PSyGenTAB: A Privacy-Preserving Framework for Synthetic Clinical Tabular Data Generation via Constrained Optimization
